## What's new in Igggy 0.1.28
- **Igggy now remembers voices, and tells you the first time.** "Recognize people by voice" in Settings → People is now on by default. Once Igggy knows who someone is, it remembers their voice on this Mac and names them in later meetings. The first note where it remembers a voice says so once ("Igggy remembered Sam's voice"), with Got It, and Voice Settings to turn recognition off or remove voices. Voices stay in your library on this Mac. Let people know when you record them. - **Igggy says when Apple Intelligence is off, and takes you to the switch.** Setup and Settings → AI Models now say whether Apple Intelligence is off, still downloading, or not available on this Mac. When it's off, Turn on Apple Intelligence opens its page in System Settings, and Igggy notices the change when you come back, with no relaunch. - **Google Meet opens in the meeting's own account.** With more than one Google account connected, Join & Record and the meeting page's Join meeting link now open a Meet call in the account the meeting came from, instead of the browser's default account. - **A waiting note says when no backup is ready.** When a note is waiting for memory and no backup model can write it, the note's card now says so in words and offers AI Model Settings, instead of a grayed-out button with the reason in a tooltip. The writing queue shows "No backup ready" where Write now was. Adding a key or turning on Apple Intelligence updates both right away. - **The speaker names card works for meetings in one room.** When every voice came through your Mac's microphone, the card first asks "Which voice is you?", with a This is me button on each voice, and stays open after your first answer. An email address is never used as a speaker's name: a guest the invite left unnamed is offered as "Add a name", and the name you type is saved to People. The card's "record a voice sample" link now works. - **A one-guest meeting is named from its title.** When the invite has one guest and no name for them, and the event title names exactly one other person besides you, the note now uses that name instead of writing "Others". - **Links lead back to their page.** On a link note, the site name under the title opens the page in your browser, the note's menu in the list has Open Original Page, and new link notes keep the address at the top of Source Content. A finished link, pasted text or dropped file now opens straight into its note, without the Notes list flashing first. - **The sidebar sits closer to the page.** In dark mode the sidebar is a little darker and in light mode a little grayer, so the two modes read about equally apart. The sidebar button lines up with the window's close, minimize and zoom buttons on every macOS version, and over the open sidebar it's a plain icon, without its glass circle.
